revision_note: v1 pinned f68308d4... as THE wrong-policy output without naming an algorithm. Under jcs-n — the algorithm the P2 review concerned — no implementation emits those bytes: {"sub":{}} is the pre-normalization intermediate, and normalization then removes the emptied member. This is a SCOPING fix, not a retraction: the MUST side (1fa18622...) and the fork itself are unchanged and remain correct. Every digest below is now scoped to a named algorithm.
source: P2 finding, CPB PR#2 review (reference: draft-mih-sokolov-scitt-payload-binding-00 §3.1/§4); machine-checked in Lean 4 (jcss/Jcss/Basic.lean, jcss/Jcss/Removal.lean; every pinned byte string kernel-checked by `decide`; axiom closure {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, sorry count 0)

pipeline.jcs-n: CANONICAL-DIGEST(jcs-n, P) = lowercase_hex(SHA-256(JCS(normalize(P minus exclusion_set)))) — exclusion FIRST, then normalization, then JCS.
pipeline.jcs-s: CANONICAL-DIGEST(jcs-s, P) = lowercase_hex(SHA-256(JCS(P minus exclusion_set))) — no normalization pass; null / empty-array / empty-object members are retained.
pipeline.normalize: Absent-field normalization (§3.1 step 1): remove, bottom-up and recursively, every OBJECT MEMBER whose value is JSON null, an empty array, or an empty object. Array elements are recursed into but never removed.

must_pass.note: One digest serves BOTH algorithms: nothing in the top-level-stripped witness is null, an empty array, or an empty object, so normalization is the identity on this branch. That invariance is what makes the MUST side algorithm-independent.

must_fail.policy: exclusion applied recursively at every object level (non-conforming)
must_fail.note: jcs-s performs no member removal, so the emptied "sub" member survives into the hashed bytes. These bytes are ALSO the pre-normalization intermediate of the jcs-n wrong branch, which is exactly why they must not be attributed to jcs-n.

must_fail.policy: exclusion applied recursively at every object level (non-conforming)
must_fail.note: Recursive stripping empties the "sub" object; §3.1 normalization then deletes that member outright, collapsing the value to the empty object.

rule: Exclusion of keys is TOP-LEVEL-ONLY. A conforming implementation canonicalizing the witness with exclusion set {id} MUST produce 1fa18622... under either algorithm. A recursively-stripping implementation MUST FAIL this KAT, and its observed digest identifies which algorithm it runs: f68308d4... under jcs-s, 44136fa3... under jcs-n. The two wrong-policy outputs differ because under jcs-n the member emptied by recursive stripping is subsequently REMOVED by absent-field normalization, whereas jcs-s performs no member removal and retains it. Accordingly {"sub":{}} is never the hashed input of a jcs-n implementation — under jcs-n it is only the pre-normalization intermediate — so a diagnosis pinning it without naming jcs-s is unscoped and will not match the implementation it is meant to catch.
separation_claim: The three byte strings are pairwise distinct; machine-checked as Jcss.exclusion_depth_three_way. The fork survives normalization: Jcss.exclusion_depth_fork (bare strip policies, jcs-s bytes) and Jcss.exclusion_depth_fork_n (composed with normalization, jcs-n bytes).
digests_computed_by: Recomputed 2026-08-02 by two independent implementations that agreed on every byte string and every digest: (1) a standard-library-only Python script (hand-written RFC 8785 serializer for this subset + hashlib); (2) the CPB reference implementation cpb.canonicalize (normalize / jcs / canonical_digest) from scitt-payload-binding. Both agree byte-for-byte with the Lean-pinned strings above.
